title: Arbor Bank - Dedicated capacity discovery
summary: Discovery for Dedicated capacity. Customer runs latency-sensitive financial workflows, looking for reserved GPUs with strict data isolation and burst capacity. Main concerns: encryption, audit logs, SSO integration, predictable throughput, and cost modeling for peak month. Next steps agreed: pricing, security pack, technical deep-dive, and benchmark run.
next_steps: Send Dedicated pricing and capacity tiers (Maya)
Share SOC 2 + ISO security pack and KMS integration guide (Priya)
Schedule technical deep-dive with infra team for VPC peering and routing (Liam)
Provision benchmark environment and share test plan (Sanjay to approve data)
Follow-up call in one week to review pricing and timeline (all)
action_items: Maya Chen: Send tiered pricing + example SOW; due 2026-03-06
Priya Rao: Attach SOC2 report, encryption/KMS FAQ, and audit log details; due 2026-03-05
Liam O'Neill: Prepare sample network diagram for VPC peering + private control plane; due 2026-03-08
transcript: [00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you all making time. quick intro from our side — I'm Maya, I'm the AE on this account.
[00:09] Sanjay Patel: Hey Maya, thanks. Sanjay here, head of AI at Arbor Bank. we've got Evelyn, Tom and Janelle on as well, thanks for coordinating.
[00:18] Liam O'Neill: Hi team, Liam, I'm the SE, I'll lead the tech side, especially around Dedicated and scaling. Sorry if my audio's a bit echoey.
[00:27] Evelyn Carter: Hi, Evelyn. Cloud architect. we're exploring options for reserved inference capacity, isolation requirements, and how we can burst for holiday peaks.

[00:38] Maya Chen: Great — high level goal for today: understand your workloads, throughput and latency targets, security constraints, and timeline so we can propose the right Dedicated configuration. we'll also surface trade-offs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs private.

[00:57] Tom Reynolds: From security side I'll be focusing on data residency, KMS integration, and auditability. will, we expect to require SOC2 and SAML SSO, also looking at HSM for key storage later on.
[01:12] Janelle Morris: product here — primary use cases are real-time chat summarization for customer service and automated fraud alerts that need sub-200ms p95 for generation on short prompts.
[01:30] Liam O'Neill: okay sub-200ms p95, got it. can you share typical token lengths and QPS at peak? that drives GPU sizing and batching strategy.

[01:45] Sanjay Patel: Sure. average prompt plus completion ~120 tokens, peaks are about 1200 QPS sustained for an hour during busy windows — monthly peaks around 6 hours during close-of-business windows. baseline is more like 200 QPS.

[02:04] Maya Chen: so sustained peaks 1200 QPS — that's helpful. for Dedicated we typically recommend reserving a pool sized for base load with burst capacity configured. you can have reserved nodes plus burst that uses spare capacity or pre-warmed instances.
[02:22] Evelyn Carter: walk us through what 'burst' means operationally — is that on our account using spare capacity from Redwood or do we provision extra reserved GPUs?

[02:34] Priya Rao: hi — from product side: burst can be configured two ways: 1) burst into a shared pool Redwood manages — fast to enable but slightly different isolation; or 2) burst into pre-provisioned reserved instances you own but only pay for when used — it's more isolated but needs longer lead time. the first option is often used to handle unexpected spikes.

[02:58] Tom Reynolds: isolation is a big one for us. we can't have PII or customer data flowing through multi-tenant GPUs without controls. does your shared burst pool support customer-level encryption and audit logs?

[03:14] Liam O'Neill: good question. the shared burst path supports encrypted in-transit and at-rest, and we can ensure per-tenant encryption keys via KMS, but the control plane for that pool is still Redwood-managed. if you need physical isolation we recommend Dedicated-only nodes (no shared burst).
[03:33] Sanjay Patel: hm, may be a compliance blocker. can you do a hybrid: reserved Dedicated for sensitive traffic and route non-sensitive workloads to burst/shared?

[03:42] Maya Chen: absolutely, that's a common pattern. route PII-sensitive requests to Dedicated pool with strict routing policies; set fallback for lower-sensitivity workloads to hosted endpoints or burst pool. you get best of both worlds.
[03:58] Evelyn Carter: about network: we run in AWS in a VPC. we need private peering and customer-managed subnets. do you support VPC peering and private control plane?

[04:09] Priya Rao: yes — Redwood Dedicated supports VPC peering and a private control plane option. we also provide an on-prem package for air-gapped needs but that has longer lead time and a different support model.
[04:21] Tom Reynolds: what about SAML/SSO and RBAC for operators? we need audit trail and role separation.

[04:29] Liam O'Neill: we support SAML SSO, SCIM provisioning, and RBAC. audit logs are shipped to your SIEM and you can also export token-level logs. small caveat: some token-level traces are redacted by default — we can discuss retention policies.
[04:48] Janelle Morris: timeline — we need to pilot in Q2 and be production-ready by end of Q3. is that feasible for Dedicated?

[04:58] Maya Chen: yes feasible. typical setup for Dedicated including procurement and networking is 4-8 weeks; if you need on-prem it's longer. for a Q2 pilot we can aim to provision reserved nodes and do benchmark runs within two to three weeks if networking is pre-approved.
[05:15] Sanjay Patel: cost modeling — how do we estimate cost for these peaks? we care about predictability and unit economics.

[05:24] Maya Chen: for Dedicated you get committed monthly pricing for reserved GPUs plus a burst/overage rate. we'll send an example model with baseline reserved capacity sized for your sustained QPS and an estimated burst pool cost for peak hours.
[05:36] Evelyn Carter: also, how does caching and batching affect latency? we use session-style chat where KV cache could help.

[05:45] Liam O'Neill: with session chat we use KV cache and prefix caching aggressively — that reduces per-token work significantly. continuous batching helps throughput but can add latency; Dedicated can be tuned for latency vs throughput by setting max batch windows and prioritizing low-latency lanes.
[06:03] Tom Reynolds: any known perf numbers for 7B/13B/70B models in your Dedicated environment?

[06:11] Priya Rao: we have verified benchmarks; for example on a 13B quantized model we typically see ~80-120ms p95 on A100-class nodes with latency-optimized config. bigger models push that up. we'll attach the model performance sheet.
[06:28] Sanjay Patel: great, would be helpful to see A100 vs H100 differences. also, can you do internal performance regressions tied to our prompt set?
[06:38] Maya Chen: yes — we run evals and can run your eval set in the benchmark environment. helps catch regressions early and gives you production-like numbers.
[06:50] Janelle Morris: what about rolling upgrades and model rollouts? we need canary and A/B for safe changes.
[06:58] Liam O'Neill: Redwood supports canary rollouts, A/B tests, and automatic fallback policies. on Dedicated you can pin model versions and route a percentage of traffic to a canary.
[07:08] Evelyn Carter: key management — we prefer customer-managed keys in KMS/HSM. supported?
[07:14] Priya Rao: yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for encryption at rest and for isolating keys per-tenant; for HSM we have integrations but require a compliance review.
[07:24] Tom Reynolds: about logs and auditability — retention windows are important for us. can we configure long retention and export to our S3 / SIEM?
[07:34] Maya Chen: yes logs can be exported to S3 or SIEM; retention is configurable as an enterprise add-on. we'll include retention options in the security pack.
[07:43] Sanjay Patel: any limitations on model customization or fine-tuning on Dedicated? we plan to host private fine-tunes for fraud detection models.

[07:53] Liam O'Neill: you can run fine-tunes, but training vs inference is a different path; inference Dedicated is optimized for serving. for fine-tunes we recommend private training infra or a partner; we can support serving fine-tuned checkpoints.
[08:07] Janelle Morris: are there compliance customers in finance using Dedicated + private control plane?
[08:13] Priya Rao: yes, several banks use Dedicated with VPC peering and private control planes; some have on-prem as well for the strictest regimes.
[08:20] Sanjay Patel: okay — walk me through a sample architecture for us: reserved pool in our VPC, private control plane, burst into what exactly?

[08:30] Liam O'Neill: sample arc: reserved nodes in your VPC (we co-locate or you provision) with private control plane that manages routing. for burst you have options: burst into Redwood-managed burst pool with per-tenant KMS keys (faster) OR pre-provisioned warm instances that you only enable during peaks. the tradeoff is isolation versus time-to-burst.
[08:51] Tom Reynolds: if we do the Redwood-managed burst pool, how do you guarantee data don't persist beyond our retention?

[08:59] Priya Rao: we enforce short-lived cache and ephemeral storage, and we can set retention policies; logs and telemetry retention are configurable and we can contractually commit to deletion windows.
[09:12] Sanjay Patel: network egress charges — who bears them if burst is in Redwood-managed infra?
[09:20] Maya Chen: typically Redwood covers internal routing; public egress to your network/cloud is billed according to contract. we'll put an example in the pricing attachment.
[09:31] Janelle Morris: can we do a pilot with a small reserved pool (e.g., 4 GPUs) and then test bursting to 20 GPUs during peak events?
[09:39] Liam O'Neill: yes that's a common pilot — 4 reserved for baseline, and a burst target for peak. we'll help size the GPUs (A100/H100) based on your QPS and latency targets.
[09:50] Evelyn Carter: provisioning lead times for H100 are longer, right?
[09:54] Priya Rao: correct — H100 inventory varies; we can usually provision A100 faster. if you need guaranteed H100 capacity we recommend an early reservation.
[10:03] Tom Reynolds: security review — what artifacts can you share quickly so our compliance team can triage?
[10:10] Maya Chen: we'll share SOC2 Type II, ISO docs, network diagram, KMS integration guide, and a short security FAQ. Priya will attach them.
[10:20] Priya Rao: I'll send the pack after this call — includes sample contractual language for data residency and deletion clauses.
[10:27] Sanjay Patel: great. for the benchmark run we will need a test harness and an NDA for sample data, can you support that?
[10:36] Maya Chen: yes we can sign an NDA and support an isolated benchmark environment. we'll coordinate on data handling and masking with Tom's team.
[10:45] Janelle Morris: ok product question: latency SLO — do you guarantee p95 latency?
[10:52] Liam O'Neill: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and we can set latency targets in enterprise SLAs for specific configs. usually we set realistic SLOs tied to model family and hardware.
[11:05] Sanjay Patel: can you route specific endpoints to Dedicated while keeping others on Hosted?
[11:11] Maya Chen: yes routing policy supports per-endpoint, per-customer, and per-model rules. you can tag routes as PII-sensitive and pin them to Dedicated.
[11:22] Tom Reynolds: about encryption keys — do you rotate keys automatically?
[11:27] Priya Rao: yes, we support key rotation policies and you can enforce CMK rotation schedules with your KMS.
[11:35] Evelyn Carter: upsides and tradeoffs summary please — reserved vs burst vs private?

[11:41] Liam O'Neill: reserved = predictable cost and isolation; burst managed pool = elastic, fast to enable but slightly less physical isolation; private/on-prem = highest isolation and control but longest setup and higher op overhead.
[11:56] Sanjay Patel: ok let's talk numbers — can we get a sample cost model for 4x A100 reserved with 16 GPU burst available for 6 peak hours per month?
[12:07] Maya Chen: yes, we'll prepare a scenario-based TCO and include model-level perf assumptions. expect delivery in the pricing attachment by EOD next business day.
[12:18] Janelle Morris: what's the expected escalation process if we hit a major outage?
[12:24] Priya Rao: enterprise customers get 24/7 support with on-call SEs, incident playbooks, and designated CSM. for Dedicated we also have proactive monitoring and early-warning traces.
[12:35] Tom Reynolds: any references or customers in our space you can point to?
[12:40] Maya Chen: we can share anonymized references of regional banks and payments customers on Dedicated. we'll include a short case study in the follow-up.
[12:51] Sanjay Patel: perfect. final thing — do you have any constraints around model families? can we bring our own model weights?

[12:59] Liam O'Neill: you can bring your own model checkpoints for serving; we support common formats and will help with quantization and kernel selection. some enterprise customers host sensitive checkpoints in their VPC for extra control.
[13:12] Evelyn Carter: sounds good. next steps recap?

[13:16] Maya Chen: recap: 1) we'll send pricing + SOW example, 2) Priya sends security pack, 3) Liam to draft network diagram and pilot sizing, 4) we'll schedule a technical deep-dive next week to kick off benchmark — does that work?
[13:29] Sanjay Patel: yes, that works. I will circulate a decision matrix and approve dataset for benchmarking this week.
[13:36] Janelle Morris: one more question — latency when KV cache hits, do you have numbers?
[13:41] Liam O'Neill: KV cache hits can reduce p95 by 30-60% depending on reuse. we'll include sample numbers from similar chat workloads.
[13:51] Tom Reynolds: great. thanks everyone — we'll await the security pack and pricing. let's put a follow-up on calendar for next Thursday.
[14:00] Maya Chen: thanks all, appreciate it. we'll circulate notes and next steps after the call.
[14:06] (call ends)
